title_en: Wuhan Heping Huayu Logistics Co., Ltd. v. Lechang Yuehan Steel Trading Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over third-party objection to enforcement
ruling_gist_en: When a lessor leases land to a lessee, and the land is subject to compulsory enforcement, if a non-party claims that the lessee has subleased the land to it and that it has constructed buildings on the land and enjoys lawful rights and interests sufficient to exclude the enforcement, it may assert its rights through an action of execution objection by a non-party. When a people's court hears a case where a sub-lessee files an action of execution objection as a non-party, it must both protect the legitimate rights of the sub-lessee in accordance with the law and prevent it from abusing the action of execution objection by a non-party, thereby hindering the normal conduct of compulsory enforcement proceedings. Whether the execution objection raised by the sub-lessee can exclude compulsory enforcement shall be examined in accordance with Article 311 (Article 309 after amendment) of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

full_text_en:
Wuhan Heping Huayu Logistics Co., Ltd. v. Lechang Yuehan Steel Trade Co., Ltd., et al. — action for execution objection by a third party

【Ruling Summary】

Where a lessor leases land to a lessee, and when the land is subjected to compulsory enforcement, a third party who claims that the lessee subleased the land to it and that it has constructed buildings on the land and enjoys lawful rights and interests sufficient to preclude compulsory enforcement may assert its rights through an action for execution objection by a third party. When a people's court hears an action for execution objection filed by a sublessee as a third party, it shall, on the one hand, protect the legitimate rights of the sublessee in accordance with the law, and on the other hand, prevent the sublessee from abusing the action for execution objection by a third party to obstruct the normal process of compulsory enforcement. Whether the sublessee's execution objection can preclude compulsory enforcement shall be examined in accordance with the provisions of Article 311 (Article 309 after amendment) of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

Supreme People's Court
Civil Judgment

(2019) Supreme People's Court Final Civil No. 1790

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Wuhan Heping Huayu Logistics Co., Ltd. Domicile: Gongjialing, Donghu Ecotourism Scenic Area, Wuhan City, Hubei Province.

Legal Representative: Li Di, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Wang Fang, lawyer of Hubei Zhuosheng Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Lechang Yuehan Steel Trade Co., Ltd. Domicile: Unit 02, First Floor, Block B, Xingfujiayuan, Zhanqian Road, Lechang City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Sun Guangliang, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Xu Qiulin, lawyer of Hubei Qianshun Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Mei Zhanchun, lawyer of Hubei Hanfeng Law Firm.

Third Party at First Instance: Wuhan Huayu Li's Business and Trade Group Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 235, Qingwang Road, Gongjialing, Heping Township, Donghu Ecotourism Scenic Area, Wuhan City, Hubei Province.

Legal Representative: Li Shaohua, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Chen Jing, lawyer of Hubei Huifenghe Law Firm.

Third Party at First Instance: Li Shaohua, male, born January 23, 1971, Han ethnicity, domiciled in Hongshan District, Wuhan City, Hubei Province.

Agent ad litem: Chen Jing, lawyer of Hubei Huifenghe Law Firm.

The appellant, Wuhan Heping Huayu Logistics Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huayu Logistics Company), brought an appeal against the civil judgment (2018) E Civil First Instance No. 99 rendered by the Hubei High People's Court regarding the action for execution objection by a third party involving the appellee, Lechang Yuehan Steel Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yuehan Steel Company), and the third parties at first instance, Wuhan Huayu Li's Business and Trade Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huayu Li's Company) and Li Shaohua, to this Court. After docketing the case on October 10, 2019, this Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a hearing. The agent ad litem of the appellant Huayu Logistics Company, Wang Fang; the agents ad litem of the appellee Yuehan Steel Company, Xu Qiulin and Mei Zhanchun; the legal representative of the third party at first instance Huayu Li's Company, Li Shaohua, and its agent ad litem, Chen Jing; and the third party at first instance Li Shaohua and his agent ad litem, Chen Jing, appeared in court. The case is now concluded.

Huayu Logistics Company's requests on appeal: 1. To set aside the judgment of first instance. 2. To cease enforcement against the expropriation proceeds of the above-ground structures built on the 41.15 mu parcel of land at Group 12, Gongjialing Village, Donghu Ecotourism Scenic Area, Wuhan City, Hubei Province (hereinafter referred to as the Gongjialing parcel); to cease enforcement against the expropriation proceeds of the above-ground structures such as workshops and warehouses built on the land at No. 235, Qingwang Highway, Donghu Ecotourism Scenic Area, Wuhan City, Hubei Province (formerly the Wuhan Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory, hereinafter referred to as the Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory parcel); to cease enforcement against the expropriation proceeds of the above-ground structures such as workshops, warehouses, and office buildings of the former Wuhan Heping Zongguanyuan Industry and Trade Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zongguanyuan Company); and to lift the seizure of the said structures. 3. To confirm that the right holders of the above-ground structures on the Gongjialing parcel, the above-ground structures such as workshops and warehouses on the land at No. 235, Qingwang Highway, Donghu Ecotourism Scenic Area (Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory parcel), and the above-ground structures such as workshops, warehouses, and office buildings of Zongguanyuan Company are Huayu Logistics Company. 4. The litigation costs of the first instance and the appeal shall be borne by Yuehan Steel Company. Main facts and grounds: 1. The core issue of this case is the determination of the subject who invested in and constructed the structures in question. Huayu Logistics Company submitted sufficient evidence, yet the court of first instance failed to find that Huayu Logistics Company is the actual right holder of the structures in question, which constitutes an error in fact finding. 2. The judgment of first instance erred in finding that the design contracts, construction drawings, and construction contracts submitted by Huayu Logistics Company corresponded to ancillary works such as walls, road surfaces, slope protection, and water supply and drainage, and were unrelated to the main structures such as workshops and warehouses in dispute. (a) The scope of works expressly stipulated in Article 1, Paragraph 1 of the construction contract provided by Huayu Logistics Company in the first instance included indoor warehouses. Considering this together with the settlement documents between Huayu Logistics Company and the construction unit submitted in this appeal, and the payment vouchers for the 30 million yuan construction funds provided earlier, it can be proven that Huayu Logistics Company invested in and constructed not only the ancillary works as found by the court of first instance, but also the main structures including workshops, warehouses, and ancillary works. (b) Even if, as the court of first instance found, Huayu Logistics Company only invested in and constructed ancillary works such as walls and slope protection, such construction is not unrelated to the structures in question. Yuehan Steel Company applied for the seizure of the above-ground structures such as workshops and warehouses on the Gongjialing parcel and the Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory parcel. It is evident that the scope of seizure is not limited to workshops and warehouses but extends to all structures (including buildings and improvements) on the land. Therefore, the court of first instance erred in finding that Huayu Logistics Company's evidence was irrelevant to the seized subject matter. 3. The judgment of first instance erred in holding that "Huayu Logistics Company's claim that it enjoys substantive rights sufficient to preclude compulsory enforcement over the said seized structures cannot stand." (a) Although Huayu Logistics Company did not provide rent payment vouchers conforming to the payment method stipulated in the contract, it did provide evidence of actual investment in, possession of, and use and management of the land. Whether a sublease relationship was formed between Huayu Li's Company and Huayu Logistics Company should be substantively judged based on whether the leased subject matter (i.e., the Gongjialing parcel in question) was actually transferred for possession and use, not solely based on "whether there exist rent payment vouchers." Moreover, whether Huayu Logistics Company used the Gongjialing parcel through a sublease from Huayu Li's Company or through other means does not affect the determination of the investing entity and the right holder. Even if Huayu Li's Company subleased the land in question to Huayu Logistics Company without compensation, and Huayu Logistics Company invested in and constructed structures on the leased land, the right holder of those structures would be Huayu Logistics Company, not Huayu Li's Company. Therefore, the court of first instance erred in finding that "Huayu Logistics Company failed to submit relevant rent payment vouchers and other evidence of contract performance, making it impossible to find that a sublease relationship was established," and consequently failed to find that Huayu Logistics Company, as the investor, enjoys the right to preclude compulsory enforcement. (b) A large amount of evidence submitted by Huayu Logistics Company in the first instance proves that the assets of the Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory were transferred to Huayu Logistics Company, and after the transfer, the structures in question were actually operated and managed by Huayu Logistics Company. Due to the collective land ownership and historical reasons, the buildings on the Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory parcel never obtained title certificates. When the assets were transferred to Huayu Logistics Company, it was objectively impossible to register the ownership. The court of first instance erred in holding that "when Zongguanyuan Company disposed of the workshops, warehouses, and other immovable property transferred by the Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory, it should have registered them in accordance with the law; otherwise, no legal effect of a change in property rights would occur." The court of first instance's determination of ownership of the buildings on the Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory parcel constitutes an error in fact finding and should be corrected. 4. The court of first instance made unclear findings on whether the structures in question can generate proceeds and to whom the proceeds belong, and applied the law incorrectly regarding the determination of substantive rights in the subject matter of enforcement and the standard of proof. (a) This case is an action for execution objection by a third party. The court's scope of review should not be limited to whether Huayu Logistics Company has rights sufficient to preclude compulsory enforcement over the subject matter, but should also examine the legitimacy of the enforcement measures taken by the court against the subject matter and whether the judgment debtor, Huayu Li's Company, enjoys substantive rights over the subject matter. In this case, Huayu Logistics Company submitted a large amount of evidence covering design, construction, investment in, possession of, use of, and management and proceeds from the structures. At the same time, since the subject matter of enforcement consists of structures built on land owned by a village collective economic organization without any planning approvals, and the investment and construction took place over a decade ago, the court of first instance should not retroactively apply the evidentiary and legality standards of today to facts and evidence formed over a decade ago. Instead, it should apply the preponderance of the evidence standard under Article 108 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China to recognize Huayu Logistics Company as the right holder of the subject matter of enforcement. (b) While thoroughly rejecting Huayu Logistics Company's claim of being the right holder of the subject matter of enforcement, the court of first instance failed to explain the legal basis for seizing the subject matter or whether Huayu Li's Company enjoys substantive rights over the subject matter. Regarding the seizure of the structures on the Gongjialing parcel, the judgment of first instance did not set forth the legal provisions or factual findings on which the seizure was based. According to Article 2 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Seizure, Impoundment, and Freezing of Property in Civil Enforcement by People's Courts, "A people's court may seize, impound, or freeze movable property in the possession of the judgment debtor, immovable property, specific movable property, and other property rights registered in the name of the judgment debtor. For unregistered buildings and land use rights, the ownership shall be determined based on the approval documents for the land use right and other relevant evidence." The scope of seizure in the property preservation measures taken by the enforcement court should be limited to property registered in the name of the judgment debtor, Huayu Li's Company. However, the houses and land in question are not registered in Huayu Li's Company's name, nor are there land use right approval documents or other relevant evidence to determine that the ownership belongs to Huayu Li's Company. Therefore, the seizure measures taken by the court of first instance against the structures in question should be corrected.

Yuehan Steel Company argued in its defense: 1. Huayu Logistics Company's claim of ownership over the above-ground structures such as workshops and warehouses on the Gongjialing parcel is insufficiently supported by evidence and cannot preclude compulsory enforcement. (a) Yuehan Steel Company's application for the seizure of the above-ground structures such as workshops and warehouses on the Gongjialing parcel has a sufficient basis. Upon verification by the court of first instance, the ownership of these structures belongs to Huayu Li's Company. (b) Huayu Logistics Company submitted the Land Lease Contract dated January 1, 2010, with Huayu Li's Company, design contracts and drawings for structures, rent payment vouchers, construction contracts, sublease contracts, power supply contracts, and other evidence to prove its ownership over these structures. However, the evidence and the purposes of proof have many defects. The authenticity of the evidence is questionable, and most of the evidence cannot be linked to the subject matter in dispute. The evidence as a whole cannot form a complete and effective chain of evidence to support its claim of rights sufficient to preclude compulsory enforcement. The court of first instance's assessment of the relevant evidence was lawful and reasonable, and its findings of fact were clear and accurate. Huayu Logistics Company's evidence of ownership over the workshops, warehouses, and other buildings on the Gongjialing parcel is insufficient and cannot preclude compulsory enforcement. 2. Huayu Logistics Company's claim of ownership over "the workshops, warehouses, and other above-ground structures on the Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory parcel" and "the workshops, warehouses, office buildings, and other above-ground structures of Zongguanyuan Company" is contrary to the facts. (a) The above-ground structures such as workshops and warehouses on the land at No. 235, Qingwang Highway, Donghu Ecotourism Scenic Area (Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory parcel) have been converted into fixed assets of Huayu Li's Company. The seizure of these above-ground structures by the court of first instance was lawful and reasonable. (b) In its evidence, Huayu Logistics Company confused the 82 mu parcel of land owned by Xianfeng Village, Donghu Ecotourism Scenic Area, Wuhan City (hereinafter referred to as Xianfeng Village) with the 53 mu parcel of land owned by the Asset Management Center of Heping Subdistrict, Hongshan District, Wuhan City. It failed to prove that "the workshops, warehouses, and other above-ground structures on the Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory parcel" and "the workshops, warehouses, office buildings, and other above-ground structures of Zongguanyuan Company" belong to it. 3. The evidence submitted by Huayu Logistics Company regarding the land lease (sublease), design of structures, construction, and leasing of warehouses does not satisfy the conditions for confirming rights or precluding compulsory enforcement in the execution objection procedure. (a) The Lease Contracts submitted by Huayu Logistics Company, under which Huayu Li's Company subleased the 41.15 mu parcel in Gongjialing Village and the 82 mu parcel in Xianfeng Village to Huayu Logistics Company, have questionable authenticity. The contracts were signed before the date when Huayu Li's Company entered into the Land Share Cooperation Agreement with Gongjialing Village. The evidence of performance of the contracts is insufficient, and the objects of proof are confused. It cannot be proven that Huayu Logistics Company actually leased the corresponding land. (b) The design contracts, design drawings, and construction contracts submitted by Huayu Logistics Company cannot be shown to be related to the subject matter in dispute. (c) The evidence submitted by Huayu Logistics Company regarding the leasing of warehouses for operation and electricity supply not only lacks relevance but also cannot prove that it enjoys ownership or other substantive rights sufficient to preclude compulsory enforcement. 4. The court of first instance, based on the preservation clues provided by Yuehan Steel Company, such as the Land Share Cooperation Agreement and the Land Lease Agreement, and after lawful verification, issued a ruling to seize the property owned by Huayu Li's Company and Li Shaohua. This was lawful and reasonable and was supported by sufficient and detailed investigation materials. In this case, Huayu Logistics Company neither provided a certificate of registration of rights in immovable property nor provided any other evidence to prove that it enjoys substantive rights sufficient to preclude compulsory enforcement over the subject matter of this case. Its objection should be dismissed.

The third parties at first instance, Huayu Li's Company and Li Shaohua, jointly argued that they agree with Huayu Logistics Company's claims, and that the judgment of first instance had unclear findings of fact and erroneous conclusions.

Huayu Logistics Company filed a complaint with the court of first instance, requesting: 1. To cease enforcement against the expropriation proceeds of the above-ground structures on the Gongjialing parcel; to cease enforcement against the expropriation proceeds of the above-ground structures such as workshops and warehouses on the land at No. 235, Qingwang Highway, Donghu Ecotourism Scenic Area (Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory parcel); to cease enforcement against the expropriation proceeds of the above-ground structures such as workshops, warehouses, and office buildings of Zongguanyuan Company; and to lift the seizure of the said structures. 2. To confirm that the right holders of the above-ground structures on the Gongjialing parcel, the workshops and other structures on the Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory parcel, and the workshops and other structures of Zongguanyuan Company are Huayu Logistics Company. 3. The case acceptance fees and other costs shall be borne by Yuehan Steel Company.

The court of first instance found the following facts: On July 21, 2017, the Hubei High People's Court docketed the case of the private lending dispute between Yuehan Steel Company and Huayu Li's Company and Li Shaohua. The court rendered the civil judgment (2017) E Civil First Instance No. 49 on December 25, 2017. Yuehan Steel Company was dissatisfied and appealed to the Supreme People's Court. The Supreme People's Court rendered the civil judgment (2018) Supreme People's Court Final Civil No. 198 on April 27, 2018, which: 1. Set aside the civil judgment (2017) E Civil First Instance No. 49 of the Hubei High People's Court; 2. Ordered Huayu Li's Company to, within ten days from the effective date of the judgment: (a) repay the loan principal of RMB 1,332,322 to Yuehan Steel Company, and pay interest thereon at the annual rate of 12% from September 22, 2016, to the date of actual payment, based on the principal amount of RMB 1,332,322; (b) repay the loan principal of RMB 13,770,000 to Yuehan Steel Company, and pay interest thereon at the annual rate of 12% from January 17, 2014, to the date of actual payment, based on the principal amount of RMB 13,770,000; (c) repay the loan principal of RMB 500,000 to Yuehan Steel Company, and pay interest thereon at the annual rate of 12% from February 20, 2014, to the date of actual payment, based on the principal amount of RMB 500,000; (d) repay the loan principal of RMB 500,000 to Yuehan Steel Company, and pay interest thereon at the annual rate of 12% from February 21, 2014, to the date of actual payment, based on the principal amount of RMB 500,000; (e) repay the loan principal of RMB 3,000,000 to Yuehan Steel Company, and pay interest thereon at the annual rate of 12% from March 7, 2014, to the date of actual payment, based on the principal amount of RMB 3,000,000; 3. Ordered Huayu Li's Company to, within ten days from the effective date of the judgment, repay the loan principal of RMB 50,000,000 to Yuehan Steel Company, and pay interest thereon at the annual rate of 24% from January 16, 2014, to the date of actual payment, based on the principal amount of RMB 50,000,000; Li Shaohua shall bear joint and several suretyship liability for this; 4. Dismissed Yuehan Steel Company's other claims.

During the trial of the above case, on August 3, 2017, Yuehan Steel Company applied to the Hubei High People's Court for property preservation. The court issued the civil ruling (2017) E Civil First Instance No. 49-1 on August 4, 2017, ordering the seizure, impoundment, or freezing of property of Huayu Li's Company and Li Shaohua valued at RMB 141,763,252.11. On October 30, 2017, the court, based on the above civil ruling, issued the seizure announcement (2017) E Enforcement Preservation No. 44 and the seizure announcement No. (2017) E Enforcement Preservation No. 44-1, seizing the above-ground structures such as workshops and warehouses on the Gongjialing parcel, the above-ground structures such as workshops and warehouses on the Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory parcel, and 80% of the proceeds from the above-ground structures such as workshops, warehouses, and office buildings of Zongguanyuan Company enjoyed by Li Shaohua. The seizure period is from November 30, 2017, to November 29, 2020. On August 14, 2018, Huayu Logistics Company filed an execution objection with the Hubei High People's Court, claiming that all the above-seized property belongs to it, not to Huayu Li's Company. After review, the court issued the enforcement ruling (2018) E Enforcement Objection No. 6 on September 29, 2018, dismissing Huayu Logistics Company's objection. Huayu Logistics Company was dissatisfied with the ruling and filed an action for execution objection by a third party with the court of first instance on October 26, 2018.

The facts additionally found at first instance are as follows: On January 1, 2010, Huayu Li Company (Party B) and Gongjialing Village (Party A) entered into a "Land Share Cooperation Agreement," stipulating that: 1. Party A agreed to cooperate with Party B by providing idle wasteland of the village, with a cooperation term of twenty years, from January 1, 2010, to December 31, 2029, covering an area of 41.15 mu located in Group 12 of the village, subject to actual survey measurements. 2. Party B, regardless of profit or loss during the cooperation period, must pay Party B's land fees in full and on time each year, namely RMB 6,000 per mu per year (RMB 6,000/mu), payable in two installments per year, i.e., half at mid-year and half at year-end. After five years, the fee per mu would increase at a rate of 3%, with an increase every five years. After the cooperation term expires, the land is returned to Party A. Factory buildings, equipment, auxiliary facilities, and above-ground attachments belong to Party B. Both parties also agreed on their respective rights, obligations, and liability for breach of contract.

On January 1, 2010, Huayu Li Company (Party A) and Huayu Logistics Company (Party B) entered into a "Lease Contract," stipulating that: 1. Scope of Party B's lease. Party A agreed to lease the 41.15 mu (approximately 27,406 sqm) of land at No. 1 Gongjialing to Party B for development and construction of a warehousing and logistics center (limited to warehousing and logistics industry, not to be used for other purposes). 2. Lease term. The lease term was approximately 15 years, from January 1, 2010, to December 31, 2025, after which the contract would automatically terminate. 3. Lease fees and payment rules. (1) The land lease fee was calculated at RMB 15,000 per mu per year, i.e., the annual lease fee was RMB 617,250 (RMB 617,250), and the total lease fee for the entire lease period (15 years) was RMB 9,258,750 (RMB 9,258,750). (2) Payment rules for land lease fees. Following the customary practice of "lease first, use later," the land lease fee was to be paid every three years. That is, within three days after the contract took effect (extendable if encountering statutory holidays), Party B paid the three-year land lease fee in one lump sum to Party A (RMB 1,851,750, RMB 1,851,750). After the three-year period expired (extendable if encountering statutory holidays), Party B paid the next three-year land lease fee in one lump sum to Party A for the second time (RMB 1,851,750, RMB 1,851,750). The time limit and amount for the third, fourth, and fifth payments for each subsequent three-year period were similar, and so forth. Both parties also stipulated their respective responsibilities and agreed responsibilities.

The facts further found at first instance are as follows: 1. Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory was originally a collectively-owned enterprise under the Asset Management Center of Heping Township People's Government. On December 22, 2003, Heping Township People's Government, to promote the restructuring of Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory, signed a "Contract for Compensated Transfer of Fixed Assets" with Zongyuanguan Company, stipulating that Zongyuanguan Company would acquire all fixed assets of Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory. After the contract was signed, Heping Township transferred all fixed assets of Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory to Zongyuanguan Company and prepared an asset transfer list. 2. In March 2004, Zongyuanguan Company's shareholders, Li Shaohua and Li Anhua, jointly applied to establish "Wuhan Huayu Galvanized Sheet Co., Ltd." by contributing assets in kind. Later, upon application by Wuhan Huayu Galvanized Sheet Co., Ltd., the industrial and commercial department approved the change of name from "Wuhan Huayu Galvanized Sheet Co., Ltd." to Huayu Li Company on March 30, 2007. On May 8, 2007, Zongyuanguan Company applied for cancellation and liquidation through its shareholders Li Shaohua and Li Anhua, and the cancellation liquidation report dated August 23, 2011, showed that Zongyuanguan Company's fixed assets were "zero." 3. On June 18, 2007, the logistics and warehousing branch of Huayu Li Company was approved and established by the industrial and commercial department, with a business scope of warehousing and cargo agency (handling). On September 26, 2007, Huayu Logistics Company was approved and established with a registered capital of RMB 18 million, with Huang Huayu as the legal representative, and a bank deposit slip showed that Huang Huayu's capital contribution of RMB 5.4 million was paid by Wuhan Huayu Galvanized Sheet Co., Ltd., i.e., Huayu Li Company. 4. Industrial and commercial registration materials show that both Huayu Li Company and Huayu Logistics Company carried out logistics warehousing and cargo agency business operations. Among them, Li Weidong was both the financial officer of Huayu Li Company and the financial officer, shareholder, and supervisor of Huayu Logistics Company. Li Wenjuan was both the financial liaison officer of Huayu Li Company and the financial liaison officer of Huayu Logistics Company. 5. During the trial, Huayu Logistics Company, Yuehan Steel Company, Huayu Li Company, and Li Shaohua all had no objection to the authenticity of the satellite images submitted by Yuehan Steel Company, and all agreed that the 53 mu of land occupied by Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory and the 82 mu plot of Xianfeng Village did not overlap.

The court of first instance held that the focus of the dispute in this case was whether Huayu Logistics Company had rights and interests in the buildings involved in the case sufficient to exclude compulsory enforcement.

Regarding the ownership of the above-ground buildings on the Gongjialing plot. Based on the parties' arguments, all parties had no objection to the fact that Huayu Li Company leased the Gongjialing plot, but there was significant dispute over whether Huayu Li Company subleased the plot to Huayu Logistics Company and whether Huayu Logistics Company had civil rights and interests in the factory buildings, warehouses, and other above-ground buildings on the plot. According to Article 311 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "in an action for objection to enforcement filed by a person not involved in the case or the executing creditor, the person not involved in the case shall bear the burden of proof to show that he has civil rights and interests sufficient to exclude compulsory enforcement over the subject matter of enforcement," Huayu Logistics Company must bear the burden of proving its claim that it formed a sublease contractual relationship with Huayu Li Company regarding the Gongjialing plot and actually invested in and constructed the factory buildings, warehouses, and other above-ground buildings on the plot. In this case, Huayu Logistics Company submitted the "Lease Contract" signed between Huayu Li Company and Huayu Logistics Company on January 1, 2010, as well as evidence such as the "Construction Engineering Design Contract," "Construction Engineering Construction Contract," "Fixed Asset Loan Contract," and loan and transfer vouchers with relevant design, construction units, and banks. The court of first instance, upon comprehensive review of the evidence, found that although Huayu Logistics Company submitted the "Lease Contract" with Huayu Li Company, it did not submit rent payment vouchers corresponding to the rent amount, term, and payment method stipulated in the contract, nor other evidence of contract performance. Therefore, without other supporting evidence, the "Lease Contract" alone was insufficient to establish the fact that a sublease relationship existed between Huayu Logistics Company and Huayu Li Company regarding the Gongjialing plot. The construction projects corresponding to the "Construction Engineering Design Contract," "Construction Drawings," and "Construction Engineering Construction Contract" submitted by Huayu Logistics Company were all ancillary works such as roads, walls, slope protection, and water supply and drainage, which were inconsistent with the main buildings such as factory buildings and warehouses in dispute. Furthermore, there was no evidence to support the corresponding performance basis for those contracts. The "Fixed Asset Loan Contract" and loan vouchers only proved that Huayu Logistics Company borrowed RMB 30 million from Qingshan Sub-branch of Wuhan Rural Commercial Bank Co., Ltd. in the name of warehouse expansion, but the specific construction project corresponding to that loan contract was unclear, and the purpose in the transfer vouchers was not filled in, making it impossible to prove a connection with the above-ground buildings on the Gongjialing plot. Therefore, the above evidence was insufficient to prove Huayu Logistics Company's claim that it actually invested in and constructed the factory buildings, warehouses, and other above-ground buildings on the Gongjialing plot. Huayu Logistics Company argued during the trial at first instance that the above contracts, loans, and transfer vouchers corresponded to the construction projects of all above-ground buildings on the Gongjialing plot, Xianfeng Village plot, and Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory plot, which were uniformly designed and constructed. However, neither the specific content of the design and construction contracts submitted by Huayu Logistics Company nor the uses indicated in the loan and transfer vouchers could corroborate its claim. Therefore, the court did not support Huayu Logistics Company's claims regarding the formation of a lease relationship with Huayu Li Company over the Gongjialing plot and its actual investment in and construction of the above-ground buildings on the Gongjialing plot. Since Huayu Logistics Company failed to submit sufficient evidence to prove that it actually leased and invested in and constructed the above-ground buildings on the Gongjialing plot, its claim that it had substantive rights sufficient to exclude compulsory enforcement over the sealed-up buildings could not stand. Therefore, the sealing-up of the factory buildings, warehouses, and other above-ground buildings on the Gongjialing plot based on relevant legal provisions was not improper. Additionally, as for Huayu Logistics Company's written request to investigate and verify the authenticity of evidence A4, A15, and the RMB 30 million loan from Qingshan Sub-branch of Wuhan Rural Commercial Bank Co., Ltd., since Yuehan Steel Company and the third party had no objection to the authenticity of evidence A4 and A15, the court had already confirmed it, making such investigation unnecessary. As for the authenticity of Huayu Logistics Company's loan from Qingshan Sub-branch of Wuhan Rural Commercial Bank Co., Ltd., since the bank had already submitted the original remittance materials to the court, such investigation was also unnecessary, and the court did not grant the request.

Regarding the ownership of the buildings on the Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory plot. In this case, the "Asset Transfer List of Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory" submitted by Yuehan Steel Company showed that all assets of Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory were transferred to Zongyuanguan Company after the restructuring. Zongyuanguan Company's shareholders, Li Shaohua and Li Anhua, contributed part of the above assets in kind to establish Huayu Li Company. Later, Li Shaohua and Li Anhua applied to cancel Zongyuanguan Company. The cancellation liquidation report showed that Zongyuanguan Company's fixed assets at the time of the cancellation application were "zero." Huayu Logistics Company argued that since Zongyuanguan Company's fixed assets were zero, indicating that the company's assets had been transferred, and combined with the fact that Huayu Logistics Company was the current asset manager of Zongyuanguan Company, it could be determined that Huayu Logistics Company had legally received the above assets of Zongyuanguan Company. Therefore, Huayu Logistics Company was the actual owner of the factory buildings, warehouses, and other above-ground buildings on the Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory plot. The court held that according to Article 6 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "the creation, alteration, transfer, and extinguishment of real property rights shall be registered in accordance with the law," when Zongyuanguan Company disposed of the factory buildings, warehouses, and other immovable property transferred from Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory, it must be registered in accordance with the law; otherwise, no legal effect of property rights change would occur. Therefore, even if Huayu Logistics Company exercised management and revenue rights over the related assets of Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory, without any property registration, it could not be deemed as the actual owner of the above assets. Huayu Logistics Company also argued that the "Wuhan Housing Area Survey Measurement Form" issued by Wuhan Real Estate Surveying Center and the "Wuhan Real Estate Plan" issued by Qingshan District Real Estate Surveying Station of Wuhan could serve as the basis for determining the company as the owner of the above assets. The court held that, firstly, Huayu Logistics Company, Huayu Li Company, and the logistics warehousing branch of Huayu Li Company all had logistics warehousing business operations, and some management and financial personnel overlapped, indicating a certain affiliation between Huayu Logistics Company and Huayu Li Company. The records of "Huayu Logistics" and "Huayu Logistics Warehousing Company" in the above documents were clearly ambiguous in the absence of clear basis. Secondly, the above documents were all real estate survey documents, i.e., measuring the location, area, structure, etc., of the houses, and verification and registration of ownership fell outside the scope of the surveying department's duties. Therefore, the above survey materials could not serve as the basis for determining ownership of the disputed subject matter of enforcement. Moreover, from the analysis of the asset transfer process of Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory, the existing evidence could only prove that the above assets were partially transferred to Huayu Li Company through the operations of Li Shaohua, Li Anhua, and others, but could not prove that the above assets were legally transferred to Huayu Logistics Company. Additionally, the "Construction Engineering Design Contract," "Construction Drawings," and "Construction Engineering Construction Contract" submitted by Huayu Logistics Company were all formed after June 2008, while the factory buildings, warehouses, and other above-ground buildings of Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory existed before the restructuring in 2003. Therefore, Huayu Logistics Company's claim that it had substantive rights over the factory buildings, warehouses, and other above-ground buildings of Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory sufficient to block enforcement measures lacked factual and legal basis and was not supported. In conclusion, the court held that Huayu Logistics Company's claims and reasons were insufficient and were not supported. Pursuant to Article 227 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 312, paragraph 1, item (2) of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court rendered the judgment: Dismiss Huayu Logistics Company's claims. The case acceptance fee of RMB 750,616.26 shall be borne by Huayu Logistics Company.

During the second instance trial, Huayu Logistics Company submitted the following new evidence:

Evidence 1: "Power of Attorney of Legal Representative" issued by Ye Jiabin, legal representative of Hubei Minzu Construction Engineering Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Minzu Construction Company), stating that "the company authorizes Xu Caijin as the project manager for the factory building and supporting infrastructure project of Huayu Logistics Company." Intended to prove: Minzu Construction Company was the construction unit for the factory building and supporting infrastructure project of Huayu Logistics Company, and Xu Caijin was the actual construction person. Yuehan Steel Company submitted that: This evidence was formed before the first instance trial and does not constitute new evidence, and its authenticity, legality, and relevance are not recognized.

Evidence 2: Six copies of "Final Account of Project." Intended to prove: Huayu Logistics Company was the investor of the subject matter of enforcement and settled the relevant construction work with Minzu Construction Company. Yuehan Steel Company submitted that: Only the first page of this evidence was stamped with the seals of the construction unit Huayu Logistics Company and the construction unit Minzu Construction Company, while the rest were printed or photocopied with no page-through seal, making it suspected of forgery, and its authenticity cannot be determined, nor does it constitute new evidence.

Evidence 3: "Explanation of the Situation" issued by Qingshan Sub-branch of Wuhan Rural Commercial Bank Co., Ltd. on November 19, 2019. Intended to prove: Huayu Logistics Company borrowed RMB 30 million from the bank to pay for engineering costs such as indoor warehouses, open-air yards, road renovation, and site leveling, with the payment recipient being Minzu Construction Company. Yuehan Steel Company submitted that: The authenticity, legality, and relevance of this evidence are not recognized.

The original third parties Huayu Li Company and Li Shaohua recognized all the above new evidence submitted by Huayu Logistics Company. This court will comprehensively evaluate and determine the probative purpose of the above new evidence submitted by Huayu Logistics Company in light of the facts found at trial and other evidence in the case.

During the second instance trial, the appellee Yuehan Steel Company and the original third parties Huayu Li Company and Li Shaohua did not submit new evidence.

This court confirms the facts found at first instance.

This court holds that, based on the parties' claims and reasons, the focus of dispute in the second instance is "whether Huayu Logistics Company has rights and interests in the buildings involved in the case sufficient to exclude compulsory enforcement," and this focus involves two parts: "above-ground buildings on the Gongjialing plot" and "above-ground buildings on the Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory plot." This court evaluates the two plots separately.

First, regarding the ownership of the above-ground buildings constructed on the Gongjialing Plot. The Court is of the opinion that in this case, all parties have no objection to the fact that Huayu Li Company leased the Gongjialing Plot. However, there is a dispute over whether Huayu Li Company subleased the plot to Huayu Logistics Company and whether Huayu Logistics Company enjoys civil rights and interests in the above-ground buildings such as the factory buildings and warehouses on the plot. Pursuant to Article 311 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "where a person not involved in the case or the applying obligee initiates an enforcement objection lawsuit, the person not involved in the case shall bear the burden of proof to establish that he enjoys a civil right or interest sufficient to preclude enforcement with respect to the subject matter of enforcement," Huayu Logistics Company shall submit evidence to prove that it formed a sublease relationship with respect to the Gongjialing Plot and that it actually invested in and constructed the above-ground buildings such as the factory buildings and warehouses on the Gongjialing Plot, thereby proving that it enjoys civil rights and interests in the above-ground buildings constructed on the Gongjialing Plot sufficient to preclude enforcement. In this regard, during the first instance, Huayu Logistics Company only submitted the "Lease Contract" between itself and Huayu Li Company, but did not submit rent payment vouchers corresponding to the rent amount, lease term, and payment method stipulated in the contract, nor other evidence of performance of the contract. In the absence of other corroborating evidence, the first instance correctly held that this evidence was insufficient to fully prove the formation of a sublease relationship between Huayu Logistics Company and Huayu Li Company with respect to the Gongjialing Plot. Huayu Logistics Company also submitted evidence such as the "Construction Engineering Design Contract," "Construction Drawings," and "Construction Engineering Construction Contract" during the first instance. However, the first instance also found and held that the engineering projects corresponding to the above evidence were ancillary works of structures such as road surfaces, enclosing walls, slope protection, and water supply and drainage, which were inconsistent with the main buildings involved in the case, such as the factory buildings and warehouses. Moreover, there was no other evidence to corroborate that the corresponding performance basis corresponded to the above contracts. The "Fixed Asset Loan Contract" and loan vouchers submitted by Huayu Logistics Company in the first instance could only prove that Huayu Logistics Company borrowed RMB 30,000,000 from Wuhan Rural Commercial Bank Qingshan Branch in the name of warehouse expansion. However, the specific engineering project corresponding to the loan contract was unclear, and the "purpose" field in the transfer vouchers was left blank, making it impossible to prove a connection with the above-ground buildings on the Gongjialing Plot. During the second instance of this Court, Huayu Logistics Company submitted additional evidence such as the "Project Settlement Statement," "Power of Attorney for Legal Representative," and "Explanation of Circumstances" to support its claims. Because the first instance had already found that the engineering projects corresponding to the evidence such as the "Construction Engineering Design Contract," "Construction Drawings," and "Construction Engineering Construction Contract" submitted by Huayu Logistics Company in the first instance were ancillary works of structures such as road surfaces, enclosing walls, slope protection, and water supply and drainage, inconsistent with the main buildings involved in the case such as the factory buildings and warehouses, even if the "Project Settlement Statement" and "Power of Attorney for Legal Representative" submitted by Huayu Logistics Company were authentic, this could not prove that Huayu Logistics Company invested in and constructed the main buildings involved in the case such as the factory buildings and warehouses. The "Explanation of Circumstances" showed that the reason for Huayu Logistics Company's application for the loan from Wuhan Rural Commercial Bank Qingshan Branch was to pay engineering costs for the transformation of indoor warehouse open-air freight yard roads and site-leveling works; this still could not prove that the loan was actually used for the construction of the buildings involved in the case such as the factory buildings and warehouses. Therefore, the above new evidence submitted by Huayu Logistics Company was also insufficient to prove that it invested in and constructed the buildings on the Gongjialing Plot. Accordingly, the first instance was not improper in finding that the evidence submitted by Huayu Logistics Company could not prove that it enjoyed civil rights and interests in the above-ground buildings constructed on the Gongjialing Plot sufficient to preclude enforcement. The grounds of appeal raised by Huayu Logistics Company, such as "under the premise that it has submitted sufficient evidence, the first instance failed to find that Huayu Logistics Company was the actual right holder of the buildings (structures) involved in the case, which was an error in fact finding," cannot be sustained, and this Court rejects them.

Second, regarding the ownership of the buildings constructed on the Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory Plot. The Court is of the opinion that it has been ascertained in this case that all assets of Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory were transferred in their entirety to Zongguanyuan Company after the restructuring. Shareholders Li Shaohua and Li Anhua of Zongguanyuan Company contributed part of the above assets in kind as capital contributions to establish Huayu Li Company. The existing evidence submitted by Huayu Logistics Company cannot prove that the immovable property such as factory buildings and warehouses transferred by Zongguanyuan Company in the process of disposing of Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory has been legally registered for changes in ownership. Therefore, even if Huayu Logistics Company exercised rights to manage and receive benefits from the relevant assets of Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory, in the absence of relevant ownership registration certificates, the existing evidence submitted by Huayu Logistics Company cannot prove that Huayu Logistics Company is the actual right holder of the above assets. It has also been ascertained in this case that the above-ground buildings such as the factory buildings and warehouses of Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory already existed before the restructuring of Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory in 2003. The "Construction Engineering Design Contract," "Construction Drawings," and "Construction Engineering Construction Contract" submitted by Huayu Logistics Company in the first instance were all formed after June 2008, later than the time when the above-ground buildings of Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory were formed. Moreover, the corresponding engineering projects were ancillary works of structures such as road surfaces, enclosing walls, slope protection, and water supply and drainage, inconsistent with the main buildings involved in the case such as the factory buildings and warehouses. Even though Huayu Logistics Company submitted additional evidence such as the "Project Settlement Statement," "Power of Attorney for Legal Representative," and "Explanation of Circumstances" during the second instance of this case, it still could not form a complete chain of evidence to prove that it was the actual right holder of the relevant assets of Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory. Therefore, the first instance's factual finding that Huayu Logistics Company does not enjoy substantive rights in the above-ground buildings such as the factory buildings and warehouses of Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory and that such rights are insufficient to block enforcement is also not improper. It is correct that the first instance did not support Huayu Logistics Company's claim that "it is the actual right holder of the above assets," and this Court affirms that. Regarding Huayu Logistics Company's claim that the "Wuhan Housing Area Investigation and Measurement Form" issued by the Wuhan Real Estate Survey and Mapping Center and the "Wuhan Real Estate Plan" issued by the Qingshan District Real Estate Survey and Mapping Station of Wuhan can serve as the basis for determining that the company is the owner of the above assets. The first instance has already found that Huayu Logistics Company, Huayu Li Company, and the Logistics Warehousing Branch of Huayu Li Company all have logistics warehousing operations, and moreover, some management personnel and financial personnel overlap. There is a certain affiliated relationship between Huayu Logistics Company and Huayu Li Company. The "Wuhan Housing Area Investigation and Measurement Form" and "Wuhan Real Estate Plan" record the owner as "Huayu Logistics" and "Huayu Logistics Warehousing Company." In the absence of other mutually corroborating evidence provided by Huayu Logistics Company, the above records cannot clearly point to Huayu Logistics Company, nor can they prove that Huayu Logistics Company is the right holder of the real estate involved in the above documents. Furthermore, the above documents are all real estate survey and mapping documents, i.e., determinations of the location, area, structure, and other contents of the houses. The review and registration of ownership is not within the scope of responsibility of the survey and mapping department. Therefore, the first instance was not improper in finding that the above survey and mapping materials cannot serve as the basis for determining the ownership of the subject matter of the disputed enforcement. In summary, the ground of appeal raised by Huayu Logistics Company that it enjoys rights and interests in the buildings constructed on the Heping Galvanized Sheet Factory Plot sufficient to preclude enforcement also cannot be sustained, and this Court rejects it.

Regarding whether the first instance's fact findings on whether the appellant can enjoy the right to receive benefits from the buildings involved in the case and the attribution of such benefit rights are clear, and whether the application of law regarding the determination of substantive rights and interests in the subject matter of enforcement and the standard of proof is correct. The Court is of the opinion that this case is an enforcement objection lawsuit filed by a person not involved in the case. Pursuant to Article 311 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "where a person not involved in the case or the applying obligee initiates an enforcement objection lawsuit, the person not involved in the case shall bear the burden of proof to establish that he enjoys a civil right or interest sufficient to preclude enforcement with respect to the subject matter of enforcement," the scope of trial in this case is primarily "whether the person not involved in the case, Huayu Logistics Company, can enjoy civil rights and interests in the buildings involved in the case that it claims are sufficient to preclude enforcement." The grounds of appeal raised by Huayu Logistics Company, such as that the first instance court's sealing-up measure against the buildings (structures) involved in the case was erroneous and that it failed to review the legitimacy of the enforcement act, are not within the scope of trial of this case. Therefore, the first instance court's conduct in only trying and adjudicating whether the evidence provided by Huayu Logistics Company is sufficient to preclude enforcement is not improper. Pursuant to Article 312, paragraph 1, item 2 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "where the person not involved in the case does not enjoy a civil right or interest sufficient to preclude enforcement with respect to the subject matter of enforcement, the lawsuit claim shall be dismissed," the first instance, after trial, found that the evidence submitted by Huayu Logistics Company was insufficient to prove that it was the right holder of the buildings involved in the case and that it did not enjoy civil rights and interests sufficient to preclude enforcement. Accordingly, the first instance's dismissal of the lawsuit claim based on this provision is also not improper in the application of law.

In summary, the appeal claims of Huayu Logistics Company, lacking corresponding evidentiary support and legal basis, cannot be sustained, and this Court rejects them. The first instance judgment is clear in fact finding and correct in the application of law, and shall be affirmed by law. Pursuant to Article 170, paragraph 1, item 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court hereby renders the following judgment:

Appeal dismissed, the original judgment is affirmed.

The court costs of the first instance shall be borne as determined in the first instance judgment. The court costs of the second instance in the amount of RMB 750,616.26 shall be borne by Wuhan Heping Huayu Logistics Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
